A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAFEPATH study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original safety, reasoning, jailbreak, training-cost, and inference-time experiments, alongside ablations and qualitative results in Appendix D.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and adds the s1.1 model comparison and alternative Safety Trigger training-data results in Tables 4 and 6.

M1.justification: The eight-token Safety Primer, supervision restricted to the harmful-prompt prefix, reasoning-retention mixture, and zero-shot insertion procedure remain unchanged. Section 3 expands their explanation without establishing a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Section 5.9 extends SAFEPATH's training-source coverage from WildJailbreak to alternative AdvBench and BeaverTails prompts. These datasets already appeared elsewhere in v1, so they are not entirely new corpora. Evaluation tasks, languages, and attack scenarios remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated defense methods and prefix variants are retained. The new s1.1 experiment reuses the base-model, Direct Refusal, and SafeChain comparators. Newly cited approaches are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V4 adds s1.1 as an evaluated model configuration and specifies random, unfiltered sampling for the alternative training-source experiments. Existing training budgets, evaluation metrics, benchmark sample counts, and attack procedures in Appendices B–C remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 5.8–5.9 add two previously untested generalization axes: dependence on the DeepSeek-R1 model family and sensitivity to the Safety Trigger data source. These extend the robustness analysis beyond v1's retained mixture-ratio, prefix-design, placement, and activation studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. The added benchmark-average rows do not introduce an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: New Tables 4 and 6 add comparative findings about model and training-source generalization; for example, SAFEPATH on s1.1 reports 5.9 BeaverTails harmfulness and 21.3 PAIR attack success. Table 1 also changes the R-7B base-model PAIR score from 66.3 to 80.0 and adds category averages. Existing SAFEPATH benchmark scores and appendix result tables are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix B.3 retains the same definitions and five equations for NPO, reasoning retention, Task Arithmetic, and Circuit Breakers. V4 adds no theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims of lightweight safety alignment, preserved reasoning, dynamic primer reactivation, and a zero-shot variant. The headline safety reductions and training-speed comparisons are unchanged.

C2.justification: Sections 3 and 5.3 newly connect primer reactivation to 'deep alignment' and contrast it with shallow initial-token defenses. Sections 5.8–5.9 interpret the added results as evidence of model and training-source generalization. Appendix E's PAIR vulnerability and future-work limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V4 adds a model/code release statement and project URL, and explicitly clarifies that CautionPath and RefusalPath leave the reasoning block open. Section 5.6 removes the explicit eight-example explanation of the 10% mixture. Existing appendix hyperparameters, hardware, and evaluation-tool disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds references including Qi et al. on alignment depth, STAR-1, RealSafe-R1, GuardReasoner, FlipAttack, and s1. Related work now contrasts SAFEPATH's low overhead with approaches requiring curated data, reinforcement learning, or external models, while retaining the original positioning.

P1.justification: V4 rewrites portions of the introduction, training explanation, and activation discussion, adds Sections 5.8–5.9 and acknowledgements, and updates affiliations and publication information. The overall narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds two experiment tables and shaded category-average rows in Table 1. Figure 2 is relocated, Figures 3 and 8 receive color or labeling changes, and some displays are resized or repositioned. Existing plots and appendix examples retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: The added model and training-source checks broaden empirical support, while clearer supervision and baseline descriptions resolve practical ambiguities. The release statement also improves access information. These are useful but limited gains: the new experiments have sparse setup details, and the assertion that distillation artifacts are excluded is stronger than one additional model comparison establishes.
